title: KPI Outlier Playbook and Dependency Slate
content:
Purpose:
A compact operational playbook to detect KPI outliers during prelaunch ramps, map each outlier to its dependency owners, and provide a fast decision tree for go/no-go actions. This is intended to live as the short-hand for on-call product-ops and release engineers during the 2-week ramp and on launch day.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Focus on three actionable KPI families (latency/cost/error-rate, user adoption funnels, and infra capacity health).
- Define simple statistical thresholds + business impact triggers for each metric.
- Link each trigger to an owner, immediate mitigations, and fallback gating logic.
- Keep runbook steps 1-3 short enough to read in <90s.

Context / why this exists (notes-to-self):
- We have many KPI lists everywhere; this is the operational, minimal surface for decisions not analysis.
- Built from lessons in last two launches: slow mitigation handoffs, confused owners, delayed fallbacks.
- Use this doc during the run-call and hand it to SRE/serving runtime/console owners as the canonical quick triage.

Primary KPI families + baseline / triggers / owners / first response (one-line each):
1) Serving-performance (latency P50/P95/P99, token throughput, tail errors)
   - Baseline: P95 <= 280ms; P99 <= 800ms; token throughput equals capacity plan +/- 10%
   - Alert trigger: P95 > 400ms or P99 > 1.2s for >3m OR 5% unexplained 5xxs across routes
   - Owner: eng-serving-runtime (Marcus Lin)
   - First-response: switch affected route to canary-variant, enable increased batching window, notify SRE.

2) Cost-per-token and infra burn rate
   - Baseline: $/k token aligned to forecast (sheet ref in linked artifacts)
   - Alert trigger: 20%+ deviation from projection sustained > 6 hours or daily spend spike > 40%
   - Owner: finance-ops + product-ops (Priya Patel)
   - First-response: enable cost cap throttles, deprioritize non-critical batch jobs, move traffic to cheaper-compatible model.

3) Product adoption funnels (signup -> activation -> first-feature-use conversion)
   - Baseline: week 0 activation >= 18%; day1 retention >= 28%
   - Alert trigger: conversion drop > 30% relative to baseline on a cohort or abnormal drop across new users > 12 hours
   - Owner: growth (Ellen Romero)
   - First-response: roll back last client-facing change, pause new onboarding variation, open rapid UX/metrics sync.

4) Observability signal health (alerts firing, telemetry gaps)
   - Baseline: <1% missing instrumentation across routes, alert fidelity > 90%
   - Alert trigger: >3% missing spans/logs or noisy false positives (alert storm)
   - Owner: observability (Samir Kapoor)
   - First-response: enable synthetic checks, flip to fallback telemetry endpoint, escalate to SRE.

Outlier detection rules (simple heuristics we can run in the console):
- Short window anomaly: X > X_baseline * threshold for at least Y minutes (ex: P95 > 1.5x baseline for 5 minutes)
- Drift detection: rolling 24h mean drifts > 10% vs trailing 7d mean -> notify product-ops
- Spike detection: single-hour relative delta > 40% and absolute magnitude > minimum floor -> run quick decomposition (route, model, region)
- Missing telemetry: >1% of expected events missing for 3 consecutive minutes -> page observability owner.

Dependency slate (owners + latency to mitigation) — quick map (one-line rows):
- Model variant availability: eng-serving-runtime (Marcus) — mitigation: 10–30m to warm alternate variant; +1h for capacity scale-up
- Autoscale policy tuning: platform-engineering — mitigation: immediate rule flip (1–5m) for burst mode; 30m for new scaling instance to be effective
- Console / dashboard fidelity: observability (Samir) — mitigation: rehydrate dashboards, enable synthetic (2–10m)
- Billing quota / account controls: finance-and-legal — mitigation: extend quota or emergency reserve (20–120m)
- Customer comms (docs/status page): growth + comms — mitigation: publish status note and targeted emails (15–60m)

Launch readiness checklist (operational, binary checks where possible):
- [ ] All owner on-call assignments confirmed for 48h window (list updated in Jira OPS-987)
- [ ] Synthetic traffic test passed (baseline-load, spike-load) with annotated deviations <= 10%
- [ ] Smoke prompts set and validated for top 5 customer journeys
- [ ] Canary rollout schedule and automatic fallback defined in console (canary -> 50% -> 100% with auto-fallback)
- [ ] Cost guardrails configured (daily cap, token cost alerting)
- [ ] SLA rollback plan documented and owners assigned
- [ ] Communication templates pre-written (incident, partial outage, deprecation) and reviewed by legal
- [ ] Runbook printed to run-call deck and pinned in Slack channel

Decision tree (go/no-go shorthand):
- If any serving-performance trigger hits AND fallback variant available and tested, then: go with canary pause and monitor 30m
- If cost burn > 40% and cannot be mitigated by config flips within 30m: pause non-essential traffic and engage finance. Consider partial roll.
- If product adoption funnels drop > 30% and causal code change in last 24h: roll back change and pause new signups if rollback not fast.
- If observability is degraded such that >50% of relevant signals missing: delay launch until telemetry restored.

Contingency playbooks (short scripts):
- Performance tail surge: enable prefix-KV cache TTL extension, increase batching latency cap, switch route to variant with smaller model; notify upstream clients about degraded latency if >60m.
- Cost surge from unexpected embedding calls: apply rate-limiter to embedding endpoint, switch embeddings to cached responses where possible, notify product owners and enact temporary request-scoping.
- Telemetry gap: flip to fallback ingest, run historical replay to backfill if possible, mark impacted KPIs as degraded in reports.

Post-outlier retro anchors (what to capture immediately after):
- snapshot of all signals for 2h prior and 1h after resolution (export CSV + short summary)
- decision timestamp, owner who executed, and link to the play that was followed
- hypothesis of root cause (one-liner) and proposed prevention (one-liner)

Open questions / unresolved items (quick):
- Do we have a documented cost-surge SLA with finance that includes permissions for temporary capacity kills? (action: Priya)
- Should we pre-provision a second cheaper model pool for all paid launches, or only for top-tier customers? (action: product-ops to propose)
- Can SRE provide a 5-min warm start policy for model-variant swaps? (action: Marcus)

Next immediate actions (this doc is a living prelaunch slate):
- Marcus: finalize the canary rollback play and run 2 simulated failures end-to-end by 2025-03-07
- Samir: add synthetic checks for top-10 routes to observability by 2025-03-06
- Priya: confirm finance emergency quota and publish contact in the doc by 2025-03-06

Notes to reviewers: keep it lean. This is intended to be the 1-pager for the run-call and should not exceed a single screen for each on-call person. Save deeper analysis for the postmortem.

Revision history: 2025-02-14 initial draft by Priya; 2025-02-21 edits from Marcus (serving play tweaks); 2025-03-05 added dependency SLA rows and updated owners; in_review as of 2025-03-05.
